source: William Lilly Christian Astrology 1647 first edition Wellcome b30338724 PDF588–594
source_scope: Historical source interpretations, no independently verified income/wealth causal predictions and no runtime scoring promotions

groups.source_group: Following printed CXV heading and the three opening source dimensions

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXV From whence or by what meanes
claims.meaning_historical_only: Printed CXV starts lower PDF588 and concerns the source/person/method of estate or poverty, not simply the degree of wealth.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: nature of the Significators
claims.meaning_historical_only: The author first requires examining the planetary nature of each estate significator as a possible source or agent of wealth/loss.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in what houses they are posited
claims.meaning_historical_only: The houses occupied by the significators provide an additional distinct class of wealth or loss sources.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: of what houses they are Lords
claims.meaning_historical_only: The houses ruled by those planets are also relevant, not only where those planets are located.

groups.source_group: Strength grading as wealth, intermediate estate or want

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: those Significators onely give substance ... strong and fortunate
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly classifies strong and fortunate significators as sources of wealth; mere planet name is not sufficient.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators ... but meanly dignified
claims.meaning_historical_only: Moderate dignity is treated as an intermediate degree of estate rather than automatically poverty.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: unfortunate and weak Planets
claims.meaning_historical_only: Afflicted or weak planets are adverse-source candidates in the historical framework.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: oppose the moderate Significators
claims.meaning_historical_only: Opposition to moderate significators is given as an additional context for want and poverty, not an independent observed outcome.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: more copious in explaining this Chapter then in others
claims.meaning_historical_only: The author says this method warrants extended discussion; it does not itself provide any successful empirical case.

groups.source_group: Four explicitly enumerated axes for determining sources

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: First therefore consider the nature of the Planets
claims.meaning_historical_only: Planetary natures and their alleged dominion/power are the first of four methodological dimensions.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Secondly ... Signes in which the Significators are placed
claims.meaning_historical_only: The zodiac signs occupied by significators are a distinct second method dimension.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Thirdly ... Houses wherein the Significators are found
claims.meaning_historical_only: The house in which each significator is located is a separate third dimension.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Fourthly ... partill aspect of the Planets
claims.meaning_historical_only: Exact/partile planetary aspects to significators are the fourth dimension; source supplies no calibrated orb here.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: nature ... Significators ... Matters or Persons
claims.meaning_historical_only: The planetary classifications distinguish causes/activities/things from actual person categories; this distinction must be retained for all seven planets.

groups.source_group: Elemental sign/planetary-nature classifications and house matrix framing

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: The nature of the Signes are as followeth
claims.meaning_historical_only: The source turns from seven planet-person/matter pairs to zodiacal sign-nature associations.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: The nature of the HOUSES
claims.meaning_historical_only: The source next enumerates all twelve houses as categories for financial gain or loss sources.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Matter versus person and house cross-classification
claims.meaning_historical_only: A planet-related route, the sign nature and the house circumstance are all distinct layers; they should not be collapsed into a single occupation label.

groups.source_group: Count strong and weak significators before choosing cause or agent

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: to put all this into practice
claims.meaning_historical_only: The author now describes combining the taxonomy for a particular purported wealth/loss judgment rather than merely naming sources.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: from whom or whence ... obtain Wealth
claims.meaning_historical_only: The positive task is to attribute people or circumstances alleged to generate economic gains.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: from whom losse or damage shall proceed
claims.meaning_historical_only: The adverse task separately attributes agents or circumstances alleged to cause economic losses.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: consider the fortitude of the Significators
claims.meaning_historical_only: Strength of the source indicators is the first step before assigning causes or persons.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: how many of them are strong
claims.meaning_historical_only: The number of strong significators must be counted; the author does not state a numerical scoring weight.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: whether more ... well fortified or weak
claims.meaning_historical_only: Positive versus negative prevalence across significators controls how source taxonomies are interpreted.

groups.source_group: All-strong case and strengths rarely absolute

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if all prove strong and fortunate
claims.meaning_historical_only: The conditional extreme case is all source indicators favorable.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: as it seldome doth
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly acknowledges the all-favorable chart condition is rare, creating a natural default of mixed testimony.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: furtherance ... procure an Estate or Fortune
claims.meaning_historical_only: When source significators are fully favorable, the author asserts assistance toward acquiring wealth.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: according to the nature of every Planet and house
claims.meaning_historical_only: The positive wealth agent is then selected according to the planet/house classes, not whichever story sounds plausible.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Meanes given him by people, signified by those Houses
claims.meaning_historical_only: The source method can attribute gains to another person's support indicated by the relevant house.

groups.source_group: Majority-strong mixed-case and localized financial hindrance

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If all ... be not strong, but the greater part
claims.meaning_historical_only: A majority-strong but not entirely strong set requires a mixed explanation; it is not the same as all strong.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: judge according to the Signe and house they are in
claims.meaning_historical_only: In mixed cases, the original sign/house/planet classifications still determine the types of gain and loss.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: losse ... hinderance ... Planets who are weak
claims.meaning_historical_only: Specific weak significators are used to attribute loss or temporary hindrance even in an otherwise favorable chart.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: and from the houses they are in
claims.meaning_historical_only: The location of those weak planets identifies the alleged social domain/agent of harm, another separate step.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if the impeding Planet be in the third
claims.meaning_historical_only: The third house is the author's worked example of an adverse source of loss, not an empirical test subject.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Bro-ther, Kinsman
claims.meaning_historical_only: In the third-house example the author infers a sibling or kinsman, consistent with his preceding house matrix.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: may receive prejudice or losse ... not much harme him
claims.meaning_historical_only: A mostly favorable natal configuration is claimed to withstand some temporary loss; prospective rejection criteria remain unspecified.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: because of the strength of the generall Significators
claims.meaning_historical_only: The author uses strong overall indicators as a mitigating factor for specific negative economic episodes.

groups.source_group: Majority-weak and tie cases with intermittent gains and baseline class

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: all the Significators or most ... weak
claims.meaning_historical_only: A set with all or most estate significators weak is the source's general poverty profile.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: though ... at sometimes he may thrive
claims.meaning_historical_only: Temporary prosperity is explicitly permitted in a predominantly unfavorable natal profile.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: generall infelicity ... not lay up much
claims.meaning_historical_only: The predicted general long-run effect is failure to accumulate much wealth, though no window or amount is specified.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: as many Significators ... imbecill as strong
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly separately treats a tied count of strong and weak wealth indicators, rather than classifying it as one of the extremes.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: a kind of unconstant Fortune
claims.meaning_historical_only: The equal mixed profile allegedly experiences fluctuating economic outcomes.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: at this time ... increase ... at other times ... impoverish
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly allows alternating gains and losses from different people and commodities within one life.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: neither abound with Wealth ... nor ... distress
claims.meaning_historical_only: The equal-strength condition is described as neither enduringly rich nor destitute, with no quantitative threshold.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in what condition of fortune his Ancestors left him
claims.meaning_historical_only: An explicit social/family-wealth starting baseline is introduced; this must be compared to ordinary inherited socioeconomic status in tests.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: find him in the same condition
claims.meaning_historical_only: The author expects roughly unchanged socioeconomic position in a mixed case; this is a prospective-sounding claim without a measured comparator.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: neglect or ill husbandry ... diminishing Patrimony
claims.meaning_historical_only: Poor management of inherited property is allowed as a mechanism of loss, not an astrological test of personal competence.

groups.source_group: Following printed CXVI begins, navigation only

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXVI If the Native shall attain his Estate by just meanes
claims.meaning_historical_only: Printed CXVI starts after a divider in the middle of original PDF594; it concerns legal/ethical origin of money and must be extracted separately.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: resolution ... nature of the Significators ... good or evill
claims.meaning_historical_only: Only the opening of the following chapter's signifier criterion is recorded as navigation, not a proven claim for CXV.
